text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.2% today to $149.73, rebounding from a sharp 2.3% drop yesterday as oil prices climbed on Middle East conflict concerns. On October 28th, crude jumped after reports that the U.S. was preparing for potential Iran strikes following midterm elections, with geopolitical risk pushing U.S. crude to $107.89 a barrel and world oil to $115.22. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly lift profit margins and cash flow from production.

The stock's 5.2% gain over two weeks reflects the broader energy trade rally tied to Iran tensions — the very dynamic flagged in early-week coverage as a way to play the next phase of energy markets. Even as the Trump administration weighs releasing Russian diesel, analysts noted those volumes won't meaningfully ease supply concerns, leaving geopolitical risk as the dominant price driver for now.
